patches.value: Let n,m be positive integers, u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m jointly smooth, and q∈ℝ^m have Euclidean norm one. Assume for all x∈ℝ^n and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1; for every (x,t) there exists a(x,t)∈ℝ with u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a(x,t)u(x,t), with no regularity of a assumed; and for every finite closed interval J⊂(0,∞) there exists compact C_J⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,t)=q for all x∉C_J and t∈J. Define e(x,t)=||u_t(x,t)||²+Σ_{j=1}^n||∂_{x_j}u(x,t)||² and E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t)dx using Lebesgue measure, Euclidean vector norms, and the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt spatial-gradient square; Δ_x is the componentwise sum of second spatial derivatives. Prove e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable for every t>0, E is differentiable at every t>0, and E'(t)=0. No endpoint t=0 assertion is included.
